name: portune

attributes.attribute: brownie-type fairy that helps with farm work
turns mischievous by driving horses into swamps

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The portune is a British folkloric figure. It is a wizened and wrinkled being. It is a typical brownie-type fairy. It delights in helping with farm work when no payment is offered. One must resist the urge to replace its ragged old coat. The portune is useful in hauling and other heavy work. Portunes live on frog meat cooked over hot coals. The name may echo a mispronunciation of Neptune, the Roman sea god. Yet the portune has no tie to the ocean. It can turn mischievous, driving horses into swamps and laughing at their escape.

okr.objective: Describe the portune as a helpful brownie-type fairy.
